}}'''Michel Las Vergnas''' (11 January 1941 – 19 January 2013) was a French mathematician associated with [[Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University]] in [[Paris]], and a research director emeritus at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]].<ref name="ecp6">[http://www.ecp6.jussieu.fr/mlv.html Michel Las Vergnas passed away] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101022034/http://www.ecp6.jussieu.fr/mlv.html |date=2014-01-01 }}, Equipe Combinatoire & Optimisation, Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref><ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20131104102105/http://www.ecp6.jussieu.fr/MLV/index.html|title=Las Vergnas' home page}} at Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref>

Las Vergnas earned his Ph.D. in 1972 from Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University, under the supervision of [[Claude Berge]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=51552}}</ref> He was one of the founders of the ''[[European Journal of Combinatorics]]'', which began publishing in 1980.<ref>[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/european-journal-of-combinatorics/editorial-board/ List of founding editors of ''Eur J. Comb''], Elsevier, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref>

A workshop on combinatorial geometry, held in [[Marseille]] in April 2013, was dedicated to his memory.<ref>[http://www.lirmm.fr/~gioan/CG13-CIRM/public/CG13-workshop-program.pdf Workshop program], Combinatorial geometries: matroids, oriented matroids and applications, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref>

==Research==
Las Vergnas's early work was in [[graph theory]], on [[matching (graph theory)|matchings]] and [[connectivity (graph theory)|connectivity]].<ref name="ecp6"/> From 1975 he was one of the pioneers of the theory of [[oriented matroid]]s,<ref name="ecp6"/><ref>[http://www.ams.org/samplings/feature-column/fcarc-oriented1 Oriented matroids], AMS Feature Column, Joseph Malkevitch, retrieved 2013-11-03.</ref><ref name="BLSWZ">{{cite book | last1=Björner | first1=Anders | authorlink1=Anders Björner | last2=Las Vergnas | first2=Michel  | last3=Sturmfels | first3=Bernd | authorlink3=Bernd Sturmfels | last4=White | first4=Neil | last5=Ziegler | first5=Günter | authorlink5=Günter M. Ziegler | title=Oriented Matroids | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | year=1999 | isbn=978-0-521-77750-6 | zbl=0944.52006 | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Its Applications | volume=46 | edition=2nd |quotation=It seems fair to say that the major credit for the origination of oriented matroid theory should be shared by Robert Bland, Jon Folkman, Michel Las Vergnas, and Jim Lawrence.|page=150|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k2an6eBxn3kC&pg=PA150}}</ref> and with [[Robert G. Bland]] he wrote one of its founding papers;<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bland |first1=Robert G. |last2=Las Vergnas |first2=Michel |title=Orientability of matroids |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B |volume=24 |issue=1 |year=1978 |pages=94–123 |doi=10.1016/0095-8956(78)90080-1}}</ref> his later work concerned connections between combinatorics and geometry.<ref name="ecp6"/> In [[matroid theory]] he introduced the [[Tutte polynomial]] of a morphism of matroids, studied in a series of papers from the 1970s to 2013;<ref>{{cite journal |last=Las Vergnas |first=Michel |title=The Tutte polynomial of a morphism of matroids I. Set-pointed matroids and matroid perspectives |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=49 |issue=3 |year=1999 |pages=973–1015 |doi=10.5802/aif.1702}}</ref> its specialisation to graphs embedded in surfaces is known as the Las Vergnas polynomial.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ellis-Monaghan |first1=Joanna A. |last2=Moffatt |first2=Iain |title=The Las Vergnas polynomial for embedded graphs |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics |volume=50 |year=2015 |pages=97–114 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2015.03.017}}</ref> He also showed that matroids in general admit no [[tensor product]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Las Vergnas |first=Michel |title=On products of matroids |journal=Discrete Mathematics |volume=36 |issue=1 |year=1981 |pages=49–55 |doi=10.1016/0012-365X(81)90172-4}}</ref>

==Conjectures==
Several conjectures carry his name. The simplex conjecture, posed in 1980, states that every simple oriented matroid has a simplicial tope; it is known to hold for realizable oriented matroids and in rank three.<ref name="LV80">{{cite journal |last=Las Vergnas |first=Michel |title=Convexity in oriented matroids |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B |volume=29 |issue=2 |year=1980 |pages=231–243 |doi=10.1016/0095-8956(80)90082-9}}</ref><ref name="KM23">{{cite journal |last1=Knauer |first1=Kolja |last2=Marc |first2=Tilen |title=Corners and simpliciality in oriented matroids and partial cubes |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics |volume=112 |year=2023 |at=103714 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2023.103714}}</ref> 

The Cordovil–Las Vergnas conjecture, recorded by Roudneff and Sturmfels in 1988, states that any two uniform oriented matroids of the same rank on the same ground set are connected by a sequence of mutations; Roudneff and Sturmfels proved it for realizable oriented matroids.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roudneff |first1=Jean-Pierre |last2=Sturmfels |first2=Bernd |title=Simplicial cells in arrangements and mutations of oriented matroids |journal=Geometriae Dedicata |volume=27 |issue=2 |year=1988 |pages=153–170 |doi=10.1007/BF00151344}}</ref>
